I farm only 3.0 mu, and my land is in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will keep that same system this year. Because my household is large and some people work off-farm, I will choose a management style that is steady and not too labor-heavy. I have farmed for 25 years, so I do not want to take risks with weak seed or very low fertilizer. I also have well irrigation, so I will use that when the crop most needs water, rather than depend only on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and a few irrigations to protect tillering, jointing, and grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield on my small area, and I will put more nitrogen on maize than wheat because maize responds strongly when water is available. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and easier to manage in the wheat-maize cycle. I will keep pesticide use limited but not zero, because I would rather control clear pest and disease risks than lose yield.
